title: Stage 4: Sharing with ECDH and ECDSA
summary: Share an entry with another user through hybrid encryption (ephemeral ECDH, HKDF, AES-GCM), sign every share, and verify the signature before accepting it.

steps.title: Stage 4: sending a secret to someone else
body: The vault owner wants to give Bob the Wi-Fi password. Bob has a key pair; the owner only knows his **public** key. That is **hybrid encryption**:
1. make a fresh, **ephemeral** ECDH key pair (P-256) for this one share
3. `key = HKDF.DeriveKey(SHA256, secret, 32, salt: empty, info: UTF8("vault-share|<entry>|<user>"))`
4. seal the secret with AES-GCM under `key`, with a **12-byte all-zero nonce** and the entry name as associated data
5. package = ephemeral public key (`ExportSubjectPublicKeyInfo()`, 91 bytes) + ciphertext + tag
The zero nonce is safe **only** because the key is brand new and used exactly once; HKDF output from a fresh ephemeral key never repeats. Never use a fixed nonce with a key that encrypts twice.
Bob reverses it: import the ephemeral public key (`ImportSubjectPublicKeyInfo(package, out int read)`), agree the same secret with *his* private key, derive the same key, open the rest.

But anyone can encrypt to Bob's public key. So the owner **signs** each package with an ECDSA P-256 key made at `init` (`SignData(package, SHA256)`), and Bob **verifies the signature before decrypting anything**.

steps.prompt: An attacker who knows Bob's public key sends him a perfectly encrypted package claiming to be from the vault owner. What stops Bob from accepting it?
options: The signature check: it was not signed by the owner's private key
The ECDH step fails for packages from strangers
AES-GCM's tag fails because the attacker used the wrong key
Nothing; encryption to Bob's key is all that matters
steps.explain: Encryption gives confidentiality *to* Bob. Only a signature (or a MAC with a shared key) says who it is *from*. The `impostor` command in this stage makes exactly that attack.

steps.prompt: How long is a package for the 4-byte secret `p4ss`? This prints it.
code: int cipher = "p4ss".Length;   // GCM: same length as the plaintext
steps.explain: 91 bytes of public key, 4 of ciphertext, 16 of tag. The overhead is fixed, so the length printed by `share` is deterministic even though the keys are random.

steps.title: The commands
body: | `adduser <name>` | `user <name> added` (a new ECDH P-256 key pair); or `error: user <name> exists` |
| `inbox <user>` | one line per share, oldest first: `<entry>: <secret>`, or `rejected <entry>: bad signature`, or `rejected <entry>: cannot decrypt`; `inbox <user>: empty` if none |
| `forge <user>` | `forged last share to <user>`, after flipping bit 0 of the last ciphertext byte (`Package[^17] ^= 1`) of the newest share; `error: nothing to forge for <user>` if none |
| `impostor <user> <entry>` | `impostor sent <entry> to <user>`: builds a correct package for the secret `send-your-password-here`, but signs it with a *new* ECDSA key |

`share` checks, in order: locked (`error: locked`), unknown user (`error: no user <user>`), unknown entry (`error: no entry <entry>`), then a tampered entry. `inbox` works while the vault is locked: it is Bob's side, which never needs the master key. Shares stay in the inbox after being read. Unknown user for `inbox`: `error: no user <user>`.

steps.prompt: Complete Bob's side of the share.
code: byte[] key = HKDF.__3__(HashAlgorithmName.SHA256, secret, 32, Array.Empty<byte>(), info);
steps.explain: Bob imports the sender's ephemeral public key, combines it with his own private key (the same secret the sender got), and stretches that into an AES key with the same `info` label.

steps.title: Share, sign, verify
prompt: Add `adduser`, `share`, `inbox`, `forge` and `impostor` as specified. Make the owner's `ECDsa` key in `init`, and keep users in a `Dictionary<string, User>` with `record User(ECDiffieHellman Key, List<SharedEntry> Inbox)` and `record SharedEntry(string Entry, byte[] Package, byte[] Signature)`.
The keys are random, so the tests check only what is deterministic: lengths, accept or reject, and the decrypted secret. For example:
shared wifi with bob (111 bytes, signed)
Everything from stages 1 to 3 must keep working.

byte[]? keyCheck;    // stored with the vault: proves a password is right without storing the key
byte[]? masterKey;   // only in memory, only while unlocked
ulong counter;       // last nonce used; never goes backwards, so no nonce repeats under any key
string Arg(int i) => i < parts.Length ? parts[i] : "";
"status" => keyCheck is null ? "no vault" : masterKey is null ? "locked" : "unlocked",
static byte[] KeyCheck(byte[] key) => HMACSHA256.HashData(key, Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes("key-check"));
if (keyCheck is not null) return "error: vault already exists";
if (keyCheck is null) return "error: no vault";
if (keyCheck is null) return "error: no vault";
var nonce = new byte[12];                                  // 4 zero bytes, then the counter
// AES-GCM in one place. Open returns null when the tag does not verify.
static (byte[] Cipher, byte[] Tag) Seal(byte[] key, byte[] nonce, byte[] plain, string aad)
static byte[]? Open(byte[] key, byte[] nonce, byte[] cipher, byte[] tag, string aad)
// Envelope encryption: each entry has its own random data key (DEK), and only the
// DEK is encrypted ("wrapped") with the master key.
var (cipher, tag) = Seal(dek, nonce, Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(secret), name);
var (wrapped, keyTag) = Seal(masterKey, keyNonce, dek, "dek:" + name);
entries[name] = new Entry(nonce, cipher, tag, keyNonce, wrapped, keyTag);
byte[]? Unwrap(byte[] kek, string name, Entry e) => Open(kek, e.KeyNonce, e.WrappedKey, e.KeyTag, "dek:" + name);
if (!entries.TryGetValue(name, out var e)) return $"error: no entry {name}";
if (dek is null) return $"error: {name} has been tampered with";
var plain = Open(dek, e.Nonce, e.Cipher, e.Tag, name);
return plain is null ? $"error: {name} has been tampered with" : $"{name}: {Encoding.UTF8.GetString(plain)}";
if (!entries.TryGetValue(name, out var e)) return $"error: no entry {name}";
e.Cipher[0] ^= 1;                                          // an attacker flips one bit on disk
if (!entries.TryGetValue(name, out var e)) return $"error: no entry {name}";
// Changing the password re-wraps every data key. The entries themselves are not touched.
if (keyCheck is null) return "error: no vault";
if (dek is null) return $"error: {name} has been tampered with";
var (wrapped, keyTag) = Seal(newKey, keyNonce, dek, "dek:" + name);
entries[name] = entries[name] with { KeyNonce = keyNonce, WrappedKey = wrapped, KeyTag = keyTag };
record Entry(byte[] Nonce, byte[] Cipher, byte[] Tag, byte[] KeyNonce, byte[] WrappedKey, byte[] KeyTag);

// Hybrid encryption: a fresh (ephemeral) ECDH key pair agrees a secret with the recipient's
// public key; HKDF turns it into a one-time AES key. The key is used once, so a zero nonce is safe.
static byte[] SealFor(ECDiffieHellman recipient, string entry, string user, byte[] plain)

if (!users.TryGetValue(user, out var me) || me.Inbox.Count == 0) return $"error: nothing to forge for {user}";
me.Inbox[^1].Package[^17] ^= 1;                            // flip a bit of the ciphertext in transit

tests.name: share two entries and read the inbox
tests.stdin:
init correct-horse
put github ghp_secret123
put wifi p4ss
adduser bob
inbox bob
share github bob
share wifi bob
inbox bob
expect: shared github with bob (120 bytes, signed)
shared wifi with bob (111 bytes, signed)

tests.name: sharing errors
tests.stdin:
init correct-horse
put github ghp_secret123
adduser bob
adduser bob
share nope bob
share github carol
inbox carol
lock
share github bob

tests.name: a share changed in transit is rejected
tests.stdin:
init correct-horse
put a one
put b two
adduser bob
share a bob
share b bob
forge bob
inbox bob
expect: shared a with bob (110 bytes, signed)
shared b with bob (110 bytes, signed)

tests.name: a share signed by someone else is rejected
tests.stdin:
init correct-horse
put a one
adduser bob
share a bob
impostor bob bank
inbox bob
expect: shared a with bob (110 bytes, signed)

tests.name: each user reads only their own inbox, even while the vault is locked
tests.stdin:
init correct-horse
put a one
put b two
adduser bob
adduser carol
share a bob
share b carol
lock
inbox bob
inbox carol
expect: shared a with bob (110 bytes, signed)
shared b with carol (110 bytes, signed)

tests.name: passwd rewraps keys and leaves data alone
tests.stdin:
init correct-horse
put b x1
put a y2
dump a
passwd correct-horse battery-staple
dump a
dump b
get a
get b
lock
unlock correct-horse
unlock battery-staple
status
expect: password changed (key-check c219dde2, rewrapped 2 data keys)

tests.name: tampering with data or with a wrapped key
tests.stdin:
init correct-horse
put a one
put b two
tamper a
tamper-key b
get a
get b
expect: error: a has been tampered with
error: b has been tampered with

require.message: Derives the share key with HKDF
Verifies the signature before accepting a share

hints: Write one `SealFor(ECDiffieHellman recipient, string entry, string user, byte[] plain)` that both `share` and `impostor` use; only the signing key differs.
Build the package with a collection expression: `[.. ephemeral.ExportSubjectPublicKeyInfo(), .. cipher, .. tag]`.
In `inbox`, after `ImportSubjectPublicKeyInfo(s.Package, out int read)`, the rest is `s.Package.AsSpan(read)`: all but the last 16 bytes are ciphertext.
